source.title_on_document: Assessment of the Impact of Artificial Intelligence on Creative Storytelling for Enhancing the Ideation Process at the Individual Level

supplement.holds: Appendix A (Group 1 prompts to ChatGPT) and Appendix B (storytelling rubric) are inside the PDF, pp. 8-9; no separate supplement is mentioned

paper_design_summary: Ten Polytechnic students took part in a partly randomized remote experiment over WebEx, with five using ChatGPT (described as GPT-3) and five working without AI; only the four students with creative-writing experience were explicitly randomized, two per group. They completed Guilford's Alternative Uses Test (two 4-minute phases, six objects) and a 20-minute alternative rewrite of the myth of Perseus and Andromeda. AUT responses were scored for fluency, flexibility, and originality using the test manual, and stories were scored on the same traits using a 3-level rubric; participant-level total scores were compared between groups using Mann-Whitney U tests, while Graphs 1 and 2 report descriptive group sums for the components.

assignment.what_was_assigned: Membership in Group 1 (works with ChatGPT) or Group 2 (no AI). The paper states random assignment only for the four students with creative-writing experience (two per group). It does not say how the other six students were assigned, only that assignment followed a review of questionnaire answers.
assignment.quote: the four students who answered that they had some experience were randomly distributed between the 2 groups—two in Group 1 (which collaborates with AI) and two in Group 2 (which does not collaborate with AI)

task.description: Two tasks done by the same participants: (1) Guilford's Alternative Uses Test (divergent_test), up to six alternative uses for each of 6 everyday objects; (2) creative storytelling (creative_writing) with the 'Pattern Modification and Subversion Technique', writing an alternative version of the myth of Perseus and Andromeda.
task.duration: AUT: two phases of 4 minutes each; storytelling: 20 minutes (p. 3, Section 3.2)

eligibility.reason: Ten students analyzed, five per group (p. 2, Section 3.1; p. 5, Table 3; p. 6, Table 5), below the 50-person threshold. Random assignment is explicitly stated only for the four students with creative-writing experience, two per group; assignment of the remaining students is not stated (pp. 2-3, Section 3.1). Creativity was scored on AUT responses and narrative texts (p. 4, Sections 3.5-3.5.1; p. 9, Appendix B). List this small, partly randomized experiment in the screening report; no separate context class applies.

one_line_finding: With ChatGPT, 5 students scored higher on the AUT total than 5 without AI (mean 63.80 vs 34.40, Mann-Whitney p = .012; p. 5, Tables 3-4), but not on creative storytelling (4.40 vs 5.20, p = .329; p. 6, Tables 5-6).
